See the formula ↓

How the calculation works

Part 2 score = (Required entire-final score − Part 1 score × Part 1 share) ÷ (1 − Part 1 share)

A worked example

An 80% current grade and 85% course target, with the final worth 40%, require a 92.5% final average. If Part 1 is half of the final and scores 90%, Part 2 must score (92.5 − 45) ÷ 0.50 = 95%.

Before you use the result

The two parts must cover the entire final. Enter Part 1 weight as its share of the final, not of the course. Your current course grade must exclude both parts, including Part 1. If Part 1 covers 100% there is no unfinished part to solve for, so that input is rejected.

Results display to two decimal places unless stated otherwise. Read our calculation methodology for scope and limitations.

Frequently asked questions

Is the Part 1 weight a course weight?

No. A 50% share of a final worth 40% of the course represents 20% of the full course.

What if the final has three unfinished sections?

You can treat all unfinished sections as one combined Part 2 average if their relative weights are known.
